q: Adding 10 to every value changes the standard deviation.
why: Every value moves together, so the distances from the mean stay the same. Only the mean moves.

q: Every value is doubled. What happens to the variance?
why: The SD doubles, and variance is SD², so it's multiplied by 2² = 4.

q: The SD can be negative when most data are below the mean.
why: Myth. The SD is the square root of an average of squares, so it is never negative.

q: Which set has the bigger SD? A: 4, 5, 6. B: 1, 5, 9.
why: Both have mean 5, but B's values are further from it. SD measures typical distance from the mean.
Only when every value is the same, for example 3, 3, 3. Any difference between values makes the variance positive.
